I’m a corporate accountant.

ASC 275, which is the US law codifying risk assessment and reserves for risk, is probably the most important law concerning this IPO.

ASC 275 is the law that requires publicly traded companies to disclose known or estimated material risks. What does that mean? It means, if you’re a mortgage broker like the now defunct Countrywide Financial, you’re supposed to disclose the risks you know about. Risks like knowingly selling mortgages to people who can’t afford them and are likely to default.

You’re also, by law, supposed to set aside a reserve to cover losses stemming from such risks. If you’re an oil company, for example, you’re required to set aside a reserve to deal with spill cleanup and legal challenges, and you’re supposed to disclose those risks in your financial statements.

How do you even do that with an AI company? *Our product might decide to take it upon itself to exterminate the human race, or, it might take it upon itself to infiltrate government systems to manipulate markets or perform social engineering for its own ends beyond our control.* How do you possibly begin to address that risk?

In my professional opinion? It’s impossible to operate a fiscally responsible AI company. I think it’s mathematically impossible to create a sufficient enough reserve to protect the company from reasonable risks associated with its products.

That’s not including the moral question of creating a product that might kill us all.

Moreover, to position one’s self in that dialectic is to miss his point altogether and to delude ourselves with science’s efforts toward its own completion. Blake blasts Newtonian science as a “mechanism,” a belief system that inserts us into The Machine and transforms us into machines and views all creation as a self-determining mechanism that supplants God and the imagination. He deplores the degenerate state of England's imagination as it allows a depraved political system to engorge itself on the life of the chimney sweeper, who was literally sold into a life in soot-choked chimneys and discarded when he grew too large or too diseased from the coal soot. “Dark satanic mills” is a phrase that exists not only in stirring anthems but literally all across England, employing children as young as five to help run the machines. Blake urges us to break our “mind-forged manacles” and to take the future back from Mechanism as a force. Though a Blakean utopia is unlikely for us, we may use Blakean ideas in our very real struggle, our never-ending fight with those agents of our enslavement, the machines, one of which is A.I.

There was something in his absolutely glee that was fascinating. My favorite aspect of the documentary was watching different comedians approach the improvisation—others had a more “workmanlike” approach, and Saget’s open joy was another aspect that made his delivery so noteworthy. He knew exactly what he was doing.

While we were in the lobby, an older woman with her obviously adult daughter (I'm saying the daughter was a 40 year old woman) came storming out of the Aristocrats.

"I can't believe you'd show something like that here!  At this theater!  What a repulsive movie! This is Southamption!"  The theater employee was searching for words.  My buddy looks at me, "man, what movie are they talking about?"  I look up and I see it.  "Oh, the Aristocrats."  "...okay, what's that?"

I did the raunchiest four minute version I could come up with on the fly.  I wish I had taped it.  It was great.  The daughter was already embarrassed by her mom's objections so it couldn't get worse for her.  The mother looked at me horrified as I went into explicit detail about all the repulsive behaviors you can cram into that joke.  My friend is keeled over laughing.

"We call it... the Aristocrats!"

I saved that usher at the movie theater.  His smile was thanks enough.

Well, Xi's purge mania makes it clear that it is a very good thing indeed that the U.S. has a two-term limit on its presidents. While it is true that the 22nd Amendment was ratified in part out of spite by New Deal-hating Republicans who never wanted to see another Democrat like FDR get elected 4 times, the most notable impact of the amendment since ratification in 1951 is that not one U.S. president has died non-violently in office since FDR himself passed away in April 1945.

There is absolutely no good argument for having a top elected political leader or anybody else with power serve until a non-violent death or incapacitation. Name me one if you can. Has anything good arisen from seeing 3 Supreme Court justices (Rehnquist in 2005, Scalia in 2016, Ginsburg in 2020) die on the bench in this century?

No Chinese leader has been in power until death since Mao Zedong passed away 50 years ago in 1976. Objectively speaking, the half-century since has been one of the greatest and most glorious periods in the 5,000 year history of Chinese civilization. The country has changed in that time from a failed state economic basket case into a superpower. Having a clear succession procedure via what was an informal 2-term limit on the top leader undoubtedly helped.

Not sure if China will keep it up if Xi clings to power as an octogenarian or even nonagenarian autocrat a la Mao or somebody today like Paul Biya (now 93 years old) in Cameroon.

Term limits. They are good and worth keeping.

This is a tough issue for western NC. The folks who need these bridges the most are often the least able to pay for their replacement.There are probably hundreds of these bridges in rural areas around here and many of them have been rebuilt more than once after being destroyed. The power of flood waters in these mountains is awesome and it's only going to get worse in the future with increased storm frequency and intensity.

On the one hand these people are desperate for vehicular access to public roads after their bridges have been washed out. On the other hand they've chosen to live on land only accessible by private bridges. So the questions remain, who should pay for the rebuilding process, to what standard should they be built and who should be allowed to build them. 

It does seem like the qualifications for contractors to build these bridges should be relaxed to speed up the process as long as they meet safety standards. Standard bridge designs might shorten the design and construction process but terrain and hydraulic conditions can vary widely in these rural headwater areas. Creative thinking is required to develop a source of funding for the reconstruction of these bridges whwther through a state insurance program, tax fund or some other funding mechanism.

comments.name: Nits
comments.body:
Indian democracy is in a difficult situation. Modi government had promised a political ideology called Bharatiyata, which translates as Indian Nationalism that is inherently secular. But what they are actually delivering is Hindu nationalism. It is not clear who is to be blamed here, only the co-pilot or maybe both.

The co-pilot is Home Minister Amit Shah. The latest blow is the extending national song, Vande Matram. First two stanzas are written in Sanskrit, it qualifies as secular poetry depicting the geographical beauty of India. The rest four stanzas in Bengali, reportedly extended later, make it a Hindu religious hymn. 

The Supreme Court has only made one concession so far, the right to remain silent. A non-Hindu believer citizen, has been deprived of the opportunity to sing the national song for their lifetime. 

The fight is seemingly between the fair-minded people and all non-Hindus versus the politicised Hindu nationalists. But the political dynasty scion is by reckoning of many here, worse than this disease.

PM Modi has proved to be a great PM, transforming India, but constrained by geopolitical forces to take a pole position. Probably PM Modi prefers to let the Courts save the day for secular India. PM Modi had reiterated his commitment to Bharatiyata last May, after winning the West Bengal elections. I still trust that he will deliver on this commitment.

This story shows how out to lunch the so-called "progressive" wing of the Democratic party is. So Ms. Lehto would rather let Susan Collins win again, and potentially stifle Democrats' ability to stop Trump's most harmful policies, rather than accept that her preferred candidate was insufficiently vetted and wasn't actually up for the task. Even El-Sayed, who has tacked strongly to the center and kept himself above scandals, is struggling to stay ahead in a race that he should easily be winning (Benson has a 4% stronger lead for governor).

I get the disappointment with moderates. Our rep has been an outspoken supporter of Israel and routinely failed to vote with Democrats against ICE, and that was enough to keep me from campaigning for her this cycle. Everyone has their line. comments.name: Paul Horwitz
comments.body:
“Owen had only ever wanted to be a fop” is the promising first sentence of the novel (and “foppery was very much a growth industry,” the second paragraph adds), but I rather think the reviewer gets it wrong about the protagonist. The reviewer describes him as shallow and compares him to Flashman. Not quite. “Unserious,” perhaps. But he’s more in line with a fairly common Stephenson protagonist, an obvious stand-in for both reader and author, who is smart and decent enough but finds himself in bemusing, perilous, often world-historical situations and mostly rises to the occasion. I’m only a third of the way through and may be proved wrong. But so far Owen, the would-be fop, seems not so much shallow as a man with a gift for walking into situations in which everyone else knows a great deal more about what’s going on than he, and doing so with a fair amount of aplomb. 

I might add, in response to another comment, that if you can get through the first hundred pages of Cryptonomicon—I couldn’t, the first time around, although I love those pages now—the rest of the book will serve as an incalculable reward. I feel the same way about Anathem, which offers many satisfactions and surprises.

My thought about Skarsgard and the wicker suit is that he did a great job with "Murderbot", which also required a suit. Identities and mind-sets. I get it, but there’s not much depth to those. And if there’s not much depth, what are the chances of continuance?

The mind is always coming in and out with thoughts, good or bad. And an identity is a false you.

Maybe these will help you bust through the corner you backed yourself into - does that have lasting power?

When you feel better, you do better.
Feeling better sometimes means not using the “e” word. Many people hate that word. 
We are made to  move. 
But there are too many ways we can pile on  objections. Exercise is something you do to your body. Movement is who you are. 
Get in touch with that.
